subject: mathematics
title: Multiplication as repeated addition
summary: See multiplying as adding equal groups, and learn the 2, 5 and 10 times tables.

lesson.text: Multiplying is a quick way to add equal groups. The sign × means "groups of" or "times".
4 × 3 and 3 × 4 both make 12. Turning the groups round doesn't change how many things there are.
Say a table out loud every day on the way to the market or while sweeping. A few minutes a day is how you learn it.

questions.explanation: There are 5 groups of 3, so it is 5 × 3 (which makes 15).
Count in twos seven times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So 7 × 2 = 14. (9 is 7 + 2.)

questions.prompt: There are 4 bags with 5 oranges in each bag. How many oranges altogether?
Which answer is the same as 6 × 2?
questions.explanation: Order doesn't matter in multiplication: 6 × 2 = 2 × 6 = 12. 6 + 2 is only 8.
